subject: Request to extend promo credits & reactivate trial — Finexia
messages:
From: Sam Walker <sam@finexia.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trial credits expiring — can we extend?

Hi Marissa,

Quick note — our pilot with your hosted API has been going well. We started two weeks ago but our legal review and procurement slowed the team down, and the trial credits on the account are set to expire this Friday (Mar 5). Usage is around 20% of the allotment because a couple of engineers are still blocked on access.

Is there any way you can extend the promo credits or reactivate a lapsed trial for another 30 days so we can finish the evaluation? Our CTO, Tom Nguyen, is copied.

If helpful: company: Finexia; intended workload: customer support summarization + embeddings for search; expected concurrent queries ~10 QPS.

Thanks — really like the latency readings on your dashboard so far.

Best,
Sam Walker
Head of AI, Finexia
sam@finexia.com
(650) 555-0142
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Walker <sam@finexia.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@finexia.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial credits expiring — can we extend?

Hi Sam — great to hear the dashboard looks good. Thanks for the context.

I can request a 30-day extension of the promo credits and a reactivation for you, but I need to confirm a couple of things for approvals:
- Exact promo credit amount remaining and requested extension amount (do you want the same tier of credits?)
- Quick justification for leadership: is this primarily to finish the procurement/legal checks or do you plan to expand usage during the extension?
- Any compliance documents we should surface while the trial is active (SOC 2, IP handling, etc.)

If you can reply with the credit amount you want extended and whether you plan a spike in usage, I’ll loop in Rishi for the final sign-off and sort the reactivation steps.

I’ve attached the current usage CSV for clarity.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: finexia-trial-usage.csv]
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Trial credits expiring — Finexia — request for 30d extension / reactivation

Team — forwarding the ask from Finexia (see original below). They started a self-serve pilot, credits expire 2026-03-05. Sam is requesting a 30-day reactivation and equivalent promo credits so their engineers can finish evaluation while procurement wraps up.

Quick facts:
- Account: Finexia (DEAL-4859-FINEX)
- Current usage: ~20% of promo credits (see CSV attached)
- Use case: support summarization + embeddings, expected steady state ~10 QPS if they move to prod
- Requested extension: 30 days, same credit tier (equivalent to $3k in credits, approx)
- Risk: low — no PII ingestion flagged, they asked for SOC 2 docs (we have standard packet)

Ask from me: approve 30-day credit extension and reactivation (no billing changes). I propose:
1) Apply $3,000 promo credit extension for 30 days and flag account as active in console so they can continue running tests.
2) Provide SOC 2 packet link and schedule a 30-min call with Solutions to unblock their engineers if needed.

If approved, I’ll confirm with Finexia and attach a short credit-adjustment PDF for records.

Thanks,
Marissa

[Attached: finexia-trial-usage.csv]
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Trial credits expiring — Finexia — request for 30d extension / reactivation

Marissa — approved for the $3k/30-day extension. Please do the following:
- Create a credit_adjustment.pdf record and upload to the account (for billing audit).
- Mark account as reactivated in console and set a soft cap at 15 QPS for the trial period.
- Offer a follow-up 30-min call with Solutions (Priyom can lead).

Also OK to offer a conditional 5% first-invoice credit if they convert within 60 days — include that in the note to the customer. Priyom, pls confirm availability for a call this week.

-Rishi
VP, Sales Operations
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Walker <sam@finexia.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@finexia.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial credits expiring — can we extend?

Hi Sam — good news. Rishi approved a 30-day extension with $3,000 in promo credits and we’ve reactivated your account as of today. Next steps:
1) Credit adjustment: I’ve attached the credit adjustment certificate for your records. [Attachment: credit_adjustment.pdf]
2) Account reactivation: your project is active in the Redwood Console; the trial soft cap is set to 15 QPS. You should be able to run your remaining experiments immediately. Link: https://redwood.app/console/reactivate?acct=finexia
3) Compliance docs: SOC 2 packet here — https://redwood.app/docs/compliance/soc2-packet (also pushing to you via email separately).
4) Solutions call: Priyom is available Wed or Thu 11–2 PT. Would either slot work for your engineers?

Also, if Finexia converts to a paid plan within 60 days of this reactivation, we’ll apply a 5% credit to your first invoice as a conversion incentive.

Let me know which slot works for the call and if you need any additional artifacts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: credit_adjustment.pdf]
From: Sam Walker <sam@finexia.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@finexia.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial credits expiring — can we extend?

This is perfect — thanks so much, Marissa and team. We’ll take the Wed 11:30 PT slot for the Solutions call and will review the SOC 2 packet in the meantime. I confirmed the team can run the remaining experiments today.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sam
